name: staff
about: LT18, a staff interview when you hire: each line labelled with the question it means (60 his scheme, 61 a difficult player, 62 where he recruits, 63 what he wants, 69 wrapping up) or not_a_line.

card.setting: Staff interview, your office, Tuesday 9 January 2029, college
card.coach: Coach Daniels, head coach at a Big Ten school
card.them: Ray Okafor, linebackers coach at a Mountain West school

so_far.text: I've studied your film. Here's how I'd run the linebackers.
He'd recruit where you tell him to. He doesn't have a territory of his own.

options.text: Ask about his scheme and how he'd use your players (Ask)
Ask how he'd handle your most difficult player (Ask)
Ask where he recruits and who he'd bring (Ask)
Ask what he wants: money, title, play calling (Ask)
Thank him and wrap it up (End)

lines.text: Walk me through your defense. How would you use the guys we already have?
What does your front look like on third and long?
If you had our linebackers tomorrow, what would you change first?
Tell me how you teach pursuit angles to a freshman.
Show me on the board how you'd fit our personnel into what you run.
Say a kid's late to meetings three times and mouths off to a GA. What do you do?
How do you handle a star who thinks the rules aren't for him?
We've got a senior who sulks when he's benched. How would you reach him?
What do you do with a player nobody else can get through to?
Tell me about the toughest kid you ever coached and how you handled him.
Which high schools would you go after first?
Who do you know in Texas and Georgia?
If I gave you a territory, where would you want it?
Which recruits from your last stop would follow you here?
How many high school coaches would pick up the phone for you?
What's it going to take to get you here?
Be honest, do you want to call plays one day?
Where do you see yourself in five years?
What number do you have in mind, and what title?
Are you looking for a coordinator job, or would this be enough?
That's all I've got. Thanks for coming in.
I appreciate your time, we'll be in touch.
Good talk. Let's wrap it there.
Thanks, Ray. My staff will walk you out.
I think I've heard enough. Safe travels home.
